text:
Anya: Quick sync on Private delivery formats and upgrade story. Field wants a single user-facing installer + an operator option. My proposal: native packages (deb/rpm) for simple infra, an airgap tarball bundle with an installer binary, and a k8s operator for clusters. pros/cons?
Matt: deb/rpm + tarball = straightforward. operator introduces lifecycle complexity and config drift risk. we need a very small v1 API for install/upgrade/rollback.
Jess: Field feedback: one-click offline install is table stakes. also asked explicitly for a non-disruptive minor patch path (no forced downtime).
Ravi: I'd split rollout: ship installer & bundles at GA, operator as beta. v1 operator should handle install/bootstrap/upgrade; v2 adds HA and lifecycle orchestration. keeps GA scope manageable.
Sam: Security needs: airgap bundles signed + SHA256 manifest. include SBOM and artifact signing tooling. we also must document KMS/HSM integration for control plane keys.
Anya: Draft launch criteria: 1) installer for both airgap and online installs; 2) k8s operator v1 (beta ok) with documented minimal API; 3) upgrade matrix: minor = rolling, major = opt-in pause; 4) automated upgrade test harness for customer-like scenarios.
Matt: Agree. Tech risk: KV cache schema bump for some model variants. rolling upgrades will need a migration hook. add operator/install-time migration steps.
Jess: Can we expose a dry-run option for upgrades so customers can validate networking and IP handoff prior to cutover? many customers require that for change windows.
Sam: Also need Evidence of Secure Build artifacts: SBOM, signed manifest, and verification instructions. we'll tie bundle generation into existing SBOM pipeline.
Ravi: Beta program suggestion: early customers get operator beta + runbook. GA customers get installer-only path. helps limit support surface at GA.
Anya: Owner mapping: Matt -> installer + migration hooks; Sam -> security packaging + SBOM/signing; Jess -> preflight checks + dry-run tests; Ravi -> operator API + beta plan. I'll coordinate docs.
Matt: Operational target question: for rolling minor upgrades what's acceptable p95 latency bump? Field requested <10% p95 increase during upgrade. Is that achievable?
Anya: Keep target <=10% p95 for minor rolling upgrades. Major upgrades can use maintenance windows; document expected impact.
Jess: I'll author preflight checklist: disk space, required ports, NTP, entropy, backup KV snapshot, network egress whitelists, cert trust chain.
Ravi: Operator API sketch: POST /install, POST /plan (dry-run), POST /apply, POST /rollback, GET /status. Keep payloads minimal (image refs, checksum, optional window).
Sam: Security requirement: audit events for /apply and /rollback (actor, timestamp, image checksum). GA won't pass security review without that.
DeployBot: [auto] canary: private-installer-canary v0.9 -> node-01 failed: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority.
Matt: That looks like a CA mismatch in the test bundle signer. I'll re-run signing pipeline and re-push the canary.
Anya: Given the canary failure, we pause operator beta discussion for now. Voting: ship operator at GA or post-GA?
Jess: post-GA (support/training burden).
Ravi: post-GA (iterate after beta).
Matt: post-GA.
Sam: post-GA (need security review window).
Anya: Consensus = operator post-GA. Plan: finish installer, airgap bundle, upgrade hooks for GA. Operator = beta after GA. I'll draft a trimmed roadmap and acceptance tests.
Jess: I'll start the preflight & dry-run test suite.
Matt: I'll fix the signer, add migration hooks, and re-run canary.
Sam: I'll produce SBOM/signing guide + KMS checklist.
Ravi: I'll draft operator v1 API + beta rollout notes.
Anya: Follow-ups: I'll open a PR with launch criteria and acceptance tests, tag owners. Ping me if priorities shift. :rocket:
